title: Frontend: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Median of Two Sorted Arrays. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({left,right}). Both arrays are sorted finite numbers; return combined median without fully merging. Reject two empty arrays with Empty arrays. Partition the smaller array in logarithmic time.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Binary-search a partition in the smaller array and derive the corresponding partition in the other so the left side contains half the combined elements.
alternativeApproaches: Return the kth element through a related partition argument and address overflow-safe averaging in fixed-width arithmetic.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: One empty array; odd/even total; duplicates.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
